ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, A is the vertex of an angle; from A, the upper ray passes through B, the lower ray passes through D, and there is another internal ray passing through C. There are pink right-angle marks in the figure, indicating that the segment CB from C to the upper side AB is perpendicular to AB, and also indicating that the segment CD from C to the lower side AD is perpendicular to AD. Then reason: The problem gives m∠BAC = 40° and m∠DAC = 40°, so AC bisects ∠BAD. Point C is on the angle bisector AC. According to the fact that the perpendicular distances from a point on an angle bisector to the two sides of the angle are equal, BC and DC are respectively the perpendicular distances from point C to the two sides AB and AD, therefore BC = DC. Given DC = 10, so BC = 10.
